summary.p: The Maṭlaʻu's-Saʻdayn, a well-known and valuable history of the period (A.H. 716-875 A.D. 1316-1470-1) intervening between the accession of Abú Saʻíd the Mongol (b. 704/1305; d. 736/1335-6) and the death of Abú Saʻíd the Tímúrid (the "Busech" of the Venetian travellers in Persia) and accession of Abu'l-Ghází Sultán Ḥusayn. It is in allusion to these two Abú Saʻíds that this history (though it deals chiefly with the reign and career of Tímúr, who was born in the same year as that in which the first Abú Saʻíd died) is entitled Maṭlaʻu's-Saʻdayn ("the Rising-place of the two Fortunate Planets"). Full particulars concerning the work and its author, Kamálu'd-Dín 'Abdu'r-Razzáq of Samarqand, are given by Rieu on pp. 181-182 of his Persian Catalogue. Besides the authorities there cited, see my Persian Literature under Tartar Dominion, pp. 428-430. There is a good MS. in the library of Christ's College, Cambridge, marked Dd. 3. 5.
Vol. II lacks a colophon, but a note of ownership is dated 1095/1684. Written throughout in a coarse but legible ta'liq with rubrications.

revisionDesc.change: Claude (auto-merge) Merged manual/ai/multi_match/H_8.xml (one AI file describing both volumes under a single combined physDesc, e.g. "Ff. 441" for both volumes together) into this record. Vol. II's own extent (ff. 181-441) is inferred from the source's statement "Vol. I ends on f. 180"; the shared physical traits (36.8 x 28.7 cm, 31 lines, coarse but legible ta'liq with rubrications) apply to the whole 441-ff. manuscript and so were applied to both H. 8.1 and H. 8.2. Completed objectDesc/@form (was "other") and supportDesc/@material (was "chart"); added layoutDesc/@writtenLines="31". CORRECTION: the existing origin here had internally inconsistent review-flagged bounds (Hijri notAfter="1095" paired with Gregorian notAfter="1610" — 1095 AH does not correspond to 1610 CE). The AI source explains the discrepancy: this volume has no colophon, only "a note of ownership dated 1095/1684" as its terminus ante quem, which is what the Hijri 1095 bound was clearly meant to represent. The Gregorian bound was corrected from 1610 (evidently copy-pasted from Vol. 1's date) to 1684 accordingly; the "undated"/review-comment wording was otherwise left in place. Not yet reviewed by a cataloguer — please verify the corrected Gregorian date against the printed catalogue.
